source_pattern_name_zh: 新奇虚构规范/架构的严格模拟执行
activation_signals: The problem defines a fabricated ISA / storage model / encoding / numeric base from scratch (Bagua / Wuxing / a custom RISC).
The answer depends on strict spec execution; it commonly takes the form "float_precision:integer" or a specific number.
The problem contains many custom symbols, non-standard numeric bases, and unusual instruction names.
problem_signatures: 题面凭空定义了一个"八卦架构""五行架构"等虚构计算体系，给出 ISA/编码/存储规则，要求在该体系下执行程序或给出参数。
信息全部来自题面，没有外部先验；记忆中的常识反而是干扰。
答案是严格依赖规范的数值或数值:整数对。
likely_failure_modes: Replacing the spec's octal / decimal quirks with familiar binary / hex intuition.
Missing "corner" rules (special registers, exception handling, carry rule).
Simulating without a state table and letting mental arithmetic errors accumulate.

sop_phases.title: Phase 1 — Transcribe the Full Spec
steps: Transcribe the spec into a structured spec-card: {data unit, numeric base, register table, instruction set, memory model, I/O, exceptions}.
Flag every item that conflicts with x86 / IEEE-754 intuition — those are the pitfalls to watch.
Confirm the answer shape (bare number / "a:b" / long string).

sop_phases.title: Phase 2 — Build a Python Simulator (NOT mental math)
steps: Implement the ISA in Python strictly; every register / memory cell / float precision follows the spec.
If the problem provides a worked example, reproduce its output as a self-test; if the self-test fails, return to Phase 1.
For custom floating-point precision, implement the mantissa / exponent field widths explicitly — never fall back to IEEE-754.

sop_phases.title: Phase 3 — Run, Self-Audit, Format
steps: Run the simulator on the target program; print a register / memory snapshot at each step if needed.
If your intuition says the answer "should be X", double-check the spec.
Emit the answer in the exact format of the problem's example ("0.993:8", "747"); no units, no prefixes.

subtype_playbook: **Bagua architecture**: base-8, 8 channels, ISA keyed on trigrams; all arithmetic runs in octal.
**Wuxing architecture**: decimal registers grouped by five-phase attributes; arithmetic follows the spec's decimal rules.
**Fabricated RISC**: decode strictly from the opcode table; never assume x86 / ARM semantics.
output_rules: Output matches the problem's example exactly ("0.993:8" keeps both decimal places and separator).
Never replace the spec with intuition from a familiar numeric base.
